extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Aristotelian ethics / philosophy (general readers, scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting Aristotle's evaluative criteria for friendship, justice, and social relations as set out in the Ethics (types of friendship, grounds for quarrel, rules of requital, duties to relatives/elders, and analogies to political constitutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three kinds of Friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three kinds of Friendship: those based on goodness (virtue), those based on pleasure, and those based on utility (advantage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Friendship based on goodness is permanent and disinterested; friendships of pleasure and utility are fragile since the underlying motives (pleasure or advantage) may cease. Examples and consequences are discussed throughout (e.g., love grounded in pleasure vs. advantage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship co-extensive with principle of Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendant on each form of Political Constitution there is Friendship exactly co-extensive with the principle of Justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extent and nature of friendship vary with constitutional forms: paternal/kingship friendships where rulers benefit subjects, little friendship in Despotism, most friendship in Democracies because equals share more in common. This links civic justice to social bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household–constitution analogies
rubrics_metrics.description: Household relations serve as models for political constitutions: father–sons = Kingship; master–slave = Despotism; husband–wife = Aristocracy (or Oligarchy if the husband dominates); brothers = Timocracy; families without a head = Democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotle uses these analogies to show how the character of private relations mirrors political structures (e.g., Persian paternal rule is despotic). The analogy illuminates how type of rule shapes friendship/justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion in unequal friendships
rubrics_metrics.description: Between unequals the degree of Friendship and the principle of Justice should be according to proportion; those who are better should receive the greater share in respect, while the needy should receive more material benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion equalises and preserves Friendship; the superior is to be honoured for goodness, the needy to be aided for necessity. 'Not more of the same thing'—different kinds of return (respect vs profit) suit different parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fault-finding arises in utility friendships
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarrels and blame arise most naturally in Friendships whose motive is utility (advantage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because parties use one another for benefit, expectations grow and parties feel they receive less than they deserve; in contrast, friendships founded on goodness or genuine pleasure involve fewer quarrels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal vs Moral (voluntary) friendship obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship because of advantage splits into Legal (specified, contractual) obligations and Moral (unspecified, discretionary) obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal obligations are explicit and admit no dispute; Moral obligations are open-ended, produce expectations and complaints, and in some places law will not enforce voluntary dealings (trust implies forbearance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for requital: receiver's advantage vs doer's intention
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate whether requital should be measured by the actual advantage to the receiver or by the kind intention/effort of the giver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotle: where utility is motive, the advantage to the receiver is the relevant standard (the receiver should repay roughly what he gained); where friendship is based on goodness, the doer's motive is the proper standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who fixes value when no stipulation exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If no stipulation as to services/rewards is made, fairness often puts the power to fix the value in the hands of the receiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows practice (Protagoras' teaching example) and legal/ethical rationales: the trusted party must often accept the consequence of trust; the receiver should value what he received as he valued it before obtaining it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharging debts ranked above unsolicited giving
rubrics_metrics.description: Requital of benefits (discharging an existing debt) is generally a higher duty than performing unsolicited kindnesses to a companion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions arise when a new giving is more honourable or necessary (e.g., ransoming a father). Priority is context-sensitive and depends on honour and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of duties to parents, elders, and relatives
rubrics_metrics.description: One ought to assist and honor parents in preference to others; honours due to parents are analogous to honours to gods but are not identical in form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific marks of respect (rising in their presence, turning aside, maintenance) differ by relation; honours differ between father, mother, a scientist, or a general. Preference in funeral invitations and marriages is given to relatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to dissolve friendships
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendships based on utility or pleasure may rightly be dissolved when the motivating qualities cease; deceived friendships (false pretence of moral character) justify blame and dissolution; friendships with the incurably depraved may be ended though aid should be attempted if amendment is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a friend was mistaken about the grounds of friendship, he may blame the pretender. For moral change (one becomes much better), severance may be unavoidable; past intimacy, however, can allow leniency in treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past intimacy mitigates treatment after divergence
rubrics_metrics.description: When a friend changes (e.g., improves morally) and friends cease to be on the same footing, the one improved ought to remember past intimacy and allow some consideration/favors when severance is not due to extreme depravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: treat former friends with some allowance on account of previous ties; do good when feasible though full friendship may be impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship as extension of self-love and unity of soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship springs from the same feelings one has toward oneself; a friend is 'another self' — the good man is unified and so sympathises with himself and others, enabling stable friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good men wish their own good in a unified way and therefore love similar qualities in others. Wicked or divided characters lack this unity and hence cannot sustain true self-friendship or friendships with others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality increases commonality and friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Democratic equality fosters extensive friendships because those who are equal have much in common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where ruler and ruled share commonality, friendships and justice are more extensive; conversely, where rulers and ruled have nothing in common (despotism), friendship is negligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mismatched motives in love produce disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: In love-based relationships quarrels arise when the parties pursue different ends (one seeks pleasure, the other advantage), and friendship breaks when the specific motives or qualities sought are not found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the suitor who promised everything to a musician but later expects payment illustrates that mismatch of expectation (pleasure vs gain) generates conflict. If parties had agreed on terms originally, dispute less justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity norms for unequal partners: respect vs profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inequality exists, returns should correspond to the inequality: the better should receive more respect (honour) while the needy should receive more material benefit (profit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public practice reflects this (honour for those who give to the public, money for those who can be paid). Friendship requires what is possible; one gives according to ability rather than strict equivalence when full return is impossible (e.g., to gods or parents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits to friendship with slaves or instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Friendship or Justice toward things qua tools or slaves; a slave qua slave is an animate tool and attracts neither Friendship nor Justice, though qua man some principle of Justice may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotle stresses that friendship requires something in common; where none exists (tool, slave qua slave), friendship is absent, though minimal justice may exist insofar as the other is also a human being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinship-based friendship depends on origin and upbringing
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship of Kindred (parents, children, brothers, cousins) is grounded in common origin, parental relation, and shared upbringing; strength varies with closeness to the common ancestor and time spent together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents love offspring from birth (source stronger), children come to love parents after gaining intelligence, mothers often show stronger affection, brothers benefit from shared upbringing and nearness of age; common possessions (children) strengthen marital friendship.
